title: Three reds
ask: You may take from the one factory display. Which move scores the most points this round?
hint: Look for a pattern line with exactly as many empty spaces as the tiles you take.
why: A line that you fill exactly moves a tile to the wall this round. Tiles that spill onto the floor line cost points, and a line you don't finish scores nothing yet.

title: Count the cross
ask: The tile with the dashed ring was just placed on the wall. How many points does it score?
hint: Count the unbroken line across that includes the new tile. Then count the unbroken line down. Add them.
why: A tile that touches tiles across and down scores both lines, so the new tile is counted twice. Tiles that only touch at a corner don't count.

title: Take what fits
ask: Pattern line 4 already holds 2 blue. Which move scores the most points this round?
hint: Pattern line 4 needs exactly 2 more tiles. Which display has exactly 2 blue?
why: Take what your line needs. Taking more of the same colour only spills the extra tiles onto the floor line.

title: Build next door
ask: Two displays, many choices. Which move scores the most points this round?
hint: A wall tile that touches other tiles scores more. Look at the empty wall spaces next to your tiles.
why: Build next to tiles you already have. A tile that joins a line across and a line down scores both lines.

title: Least bad
ask: Only the centre is left, and you must take tiles. Which move loses the fewest points this round?
hint: You take the starting player marker whatever you do. Which colour can you place with the smallest spill?
why: When every choice hurts, count the floor line for each one. Completing a line can make up for a tile or two on the floor.

title: Top to bottom
ask: You can complete pattern line 2 or pattern line 4. Which move scores the most points this round?
hint: Lines move to the wall from top to bottom. A tile placed earlier counts as a neighbour for the tiles placed after it.
why: Order matters in wall-tiling. Here pattern line 3 is already complete, and the tiles above and below it change what it scores.

title: The last round
ask: Your pattern line 1 completes row 1 of your wall, so the game ends after this round. Which move gives the most points, bonuses included?
hint: Look at what each move completes at the end: a row is worth +{ROW_BONUS}, a column +{COLUMN_BONUS}, a full colour +{COLOUR_BONUS}.
why: In the last round, add up the end bonuses too. A full column or a full colour is worth far more than a full row, and the points the tile itself scores still count.
